stem: Which of the following nerves is the afferent pathway of the gag reflex:
fact: CN IX is the afferent limb of the gag reflex; CN X is the efferent limb.
mnemonic: IX initiates the gag, X executes it.
finding: CN IX carries the afferent gag-reflex signal.

stem: A patient complains of headaches and dizziness. Imaging reveals a tumour at the cerebellopontine angle. Which of the following nerves will most likely be affected by this tumour:
fact: The vestibulocochlear nerve is closely related to the cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory meatus; facial nerve involvement may coexist.
finding: CPA lesions commonly affect CN VIII and may involve CN VII.

stem: Regarding the abducens nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The abducens nerve innervates the inferior oblique muscle.
Abducens nerve palsy results in a vertical diplopia.
The abducens nerve originates in the medulla.
The abducens nerve enters the orbit through the inferior orbital fissure.
Abducens nerve palsy results in a convergent squint.
fact: CN VI arises from the pons, enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure, supplies lateral rectus, and palsy causes convergent squint with horizontal diplopia.
finding: The abducens reference supports the displayed convergent-squint answer.

stem: A 64 year old lady presents to ED with headaches. Imaging show a tumour compressing the structures in the internal auditory meatus. Which of the following structures are most likely affected:
options: Internal jugular vein and trigeminal nerve
fact: The internal auditory meatus transmits the facial and vestibulocochlear nerves.
finding: The internal auditory meatus contains CN VII and CN VIII.

stem: A patient complains of diplopia and on examination is found to have a depressed and abducted eye with ptosis. Which of the following nerves is most likely to be affected:
options: Ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve
fact: CN III palsy causes a down-and-out eye with ptosis and diplopia due to unopposed lateral rectus and superior oblique action.
mnemonic: III palsy: down, out, and ptosis.
finding: The oculomotor reference supports the displayed clinical localization.

stem: The trochlear nerve innervates which of the following muscles:
fact: CN IV supplies the superior oblique muscle.
mnemonic: SO4: superior oblique, cranial nerve IV.

stem: The spinal accessory nerve innervates which of the following muscles:
fact: The spinal accessory nerve supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.
mnemonic: XI shrugs and turns: trapezius plus SCM.
finding: CN XI supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.

stem: The facial nerve divides into its five terminal branches at which of the following sites:
options: At the lateral corner of the eye
At the lower border of the mandible
fact: The facial nerve divides into its five terminal motor branches within the parotid gland.
mnemonic: To Zanzibar By Motor Car, inside the parotid.
finding: The facial-nerve reference supports terminal branching within the parotid gland.

stem: Regarding the glossopharyngeal nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: The glossopharyngeal nerve originates from the medulla.
The glossopharyngeal nerve emerges from the cranial cavity via the jugular foramen.
The glossopharyngeal nerve is the efferent nerve of the gag reflex.
The glossopharyngeal nerve innervates the stylopharyngeus muscle.
The glossopharyngeal nerve supplies parasympathetic fibres to the parotid gland.
fact: CN IX is the afferent, not efferent, gag-reflex limb; it also supplies stylopharyngeus and preganglionic parasympathetic fibres to the parotid pathway.
mnemonic: IX senses the gag; X drives the gag.
finding: The glossopharyngeal reference supports the displayed incorrect statement.

stem: A 64 year old man presents to ED complaining of diplopia. The image below shows the patient's eyes gazing straight ahead. Which of the following cranial nerves is affected:
options: Ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve
fact: The source image shows a convergent squint with inability to abduct, consistent with abducens nerve palsy and unopposed medial rectus action.
mnemonic: VI lets the eye look lateral; loss turns it medial.
finding: The displayed image and explanation support abducens palsy.
